title: Happiness
summary: Happiness as the emotional state that follows from achieved values, not as a whim.

lessons.title: An Emotional State
lessons.objective: Identify happiness as an emotional state, not a possession, a rule, or a mood you invent.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what kind of thing is happiness?

choices.text: An emotional state
A physical object you can store
A political law
A duty to feel nothing

feedback.note: Happiness is named as an emotional state. It is not a thing you own or a rule you recite.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to what this unit treats it as.

feedback.note: The unit’s name for happiness is an emotional state that follows achieved values, and that state is not a whim.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s name for happiness.

feedback.note: The word that finishes the definition here is state: happiness is an emotional state.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names what happiness is.

feedback.note: The sentence to build is that happiness is an emotional state, not a whim and not an object.

exercises.prompt: Which description stays inside this unit’s idea of happiness?

choices.text: A state you feel after values are achieved
A coin you can spend later
A vote other people cast for you
The absence of every feeling

feedback.note: Because happiness is an emotional state, it is something felt, and this unit ties that feeling to achieved values.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to whether it is an emotional state.

feedback.note: Only happiness, among these, is the emotional state the unit is teaching.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two words that name the kind of state happiness is.

feedback.note: Call it emotional. Do not treat it as an object you put on a shelf.

exercises.prompt: Someone says happiness is just a whim. What does this unit say happiness is instead?

choices.text: An emotional state that follows achieved values
A whim with no tie to values
The emotional state of having no values
A prize awarded at random

feedback.note: The unit refuses the whim account. Happiness is the emotional state that follows from values you have achieved.

exercises.prompt: Build the short contrast.

feedback.note: Keep both halves: happiness is a state, and that state is not a whim.

exercises.prompt: Which word belongs in the definition beside emotional?

choices.text: State
Tool
Place
Debt

feedback.note: The pairing in this unit is emotional state. Tool, place, and debt are the wrong kind of thing.

lessons.title: What It Follows From
lessons.objective: Connect the emotional state of happiness to values that have been achieved.

exercises.prompt: Happiness, as this unit states it, follows from what?

choices.text: Achieved values
Other people’s rumors
The weather alone
Having no values at all

feedback.note: The state follows from achieved values. It is not tied to rumor, weather, or an empty list of values.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to its role in the definition.

feedback.note: Three jobs: name the state, name its source in achieved values, and reject the whim.

exercises.prompt: Complete the source of the emotional state.

feedback.note: The values have to be achieved. Merely imagined or random wishes are not the source named here.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about what the state follows from.

feedback.note: Follows from achieved values. Whims and rumors are the distractors, not the source.

exercises.prompt: A person gains a value they chose and worked for. On this unit’s account, happiness is the state that…

choices.text: Follows that achievement
Replaces the value so the value no longer matters
Shows the value was a mistake
Has nothing to do with the value

feedback.note: The emotion follows the achieved value. It does not cancel the value or float free of it.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the unit’s verdict.

pairs.right: Can be what happiness follows from
Not the source this unit names

feedback.note: Achievement is the link. A daydream has not achieved the value, and a whim is not a value achieved.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks from the unit summary.

feedback.note: Both words matter: achieved, and values. Missed whims are not the pair.

exercises.prompt: Which pairing matches the unit?

choices.text: Emotional state, from achieved values
Achieved values, from a whim
No state, and no values
A whim, from having no values

feedback.note: Keep the direction: the emotional state follows from achieved values, not the other way around and not from a whim.

exercises.prompt: Build the full short definition.

feedback.note: Happiness follows from achieved values. Leave whims and accidents out of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: If no value has been achieved, what does this unit refuse to call the source of happiness?

choices.text: The mere lack of achievement
Values that have been achieved
The emotional state itself as a name
The link between state and achievement

feedback.note: The source named here is achieved values. A gap where nothing was achieved is not that source.

lessons.title: Achievement Comes First
lessons.objective: Keep the order straight: the value is achieved, and the emotional state follows.

exercises.prompt: Which order matches the unit?

choices.text: Achieve the value, then the emotional state follows
Feel a whim first, and call that the value
Skip values and start with the feeling
Never achieve anything if you want the state

feedback.note: Follows from means the achievement comes first. The emotional state is what comes after.

exercises.prompt: Match each step to its place in the order.

pairs.right: Not the order this unit teaches

feedback.note: First the achieved value, then the state. A whim is not a step in that order.

exercises.prompt: Complete the order.

parts.text: The value is achieved, and the emotional state

feedback.note: The verb is follows. The state does not precede the achievement, cancel it, or invent it.

exercises.prompt: Build the order in one line.

feedback.note: Achieved values come before the state. After and whim do not belong in this line.

exercises.prompt: Why is chasing the feeling before any value the wrong order?

choices.text: The state is what follows achievement, not a substitute for it
Because feelings are illegal
Because only other people may have values
Because values must never be achieved

feedback.note: The feeling is the result side of the definition. Putting it first drops the achieved values the state follows from.

exercises.prompt: Match each slogan to the order it implies.

pairs.left: Gain the value, then the state
A whim is the whole story

feedback.note: Only the first slogan keeps achievement ahead of the emotional state and refuses the whim.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two time-words.

feedback.note: First and after mark the order: achievement, then the emotional state that follows.

exercises.prompt: A student says the feeling creates the value. What should you answer from this unit?

choices.text: No. The state follows from the value achieved, it does not create it.
Yes. A whim is the value.
Yes. Feeling and achievement are the same event with no order.
Drop both. Happiness is not an emotional state.

feedback.note: Do not reverse the dependence. Achieved values are the source; the emotional state follows them.

exercises.prompt: Build the warning about order.

feedback.note: The state is not first. Putting it first would skip the achieved values it follows from.

exercises.prompt: When the unit says the state follows, which item is later in the sequence?

choices.text: The emotional state
The achieved value
Neither, because there is no sequence
A whim, which is earlier than both

feedback.note: Follows places the emotional state later than the achieved value. A whim is not a step ahead of either.

lessons.title: Not a Whim
lessons.objective: Separate happiness from a whim, a feeling with no tie to achieved values.

exercises.prompt: On this unit’s account, happiness is not what?

choices.text: A whim
An emotional state
Something that follows achieved values
Something a person can feel

feedback.note: The summary adds a refusal: happiness is not a whim. It remains an emotional state that follows achieved values.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to happiness or to a whim.

pairs.left: A feeling with no tie to values

feedback.note: Happiness stays tied to achieved values. A whim is the feeling cut loose from that tie.

exercises.prompt: Complete the refusal.

feedback.note: The word to refuse is whim. State is what happiness is, not what it is not.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that rejects the whim.

feedback.note: The rejection sentence is short: happiness is not a whim. State and value are true parts of the wider definition, but they are distractors in this line.

exercises.prompt: Which feeling fits a whim rather than this unit’s happiness?

choices.text: A feeling chosen with no achieved value behind it
The state that follows a value you achieved
Any emotional state, including the one that follows values
No feeling of any kind

feedback.note: A whim here means a feeling unhooked from achieved values. Happiness is the state that stays hooked to them.

exercises.prompt: Match the claim to the right correction.

pairs.left: Happiness is whatever whim I feel
pairs.right: No. It is not a whim.
Yes. That is what it is.

feedback.note: Correct the two denials, and keep the positive claim that happiness is an emotional state.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

feedback.note: The whim is missing achieved values. Happiness is not that kind of feeling.

exercises.prompt: Calling happiness a whim drops which part of the definition?

choices.text: The tie to achieved values
The fact that it is felt
The word state, and nothing else
Nothing. A whim already means achieved values.

feedback.note: The whim account cuts the state off from achieved values, which is the link this unit insists on.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in order.

feedback.note: A whim is not achieved values. Do not swap in happiness or follows for this contrast.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence agrees with the unit?

choices.text: Happiness is the emotional state from achieved values, not a whim.
A whim is the emotional state that follows achieved values.
Only a whim counts, and values do not.
Happiness is neither a state nor tied to values.

feedback.note: Keep the whole line: emotional state, from achieved values, and not a whim.

lessons.title: The Whole Definition
lessons.objective: State the full idea in one piece: the emotional state that follows achieved values, and not a whim.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is the whole unit in one line?

choices.text: Happiness is the emotional state that follows from achieved values, not a whim.
Happiness is a whim, and values come later if at all.
Happiness is not an emotional state.
Achieved values follow from a whim called happiness.

feedback.note: The full line has three parts: emotional state, follows from achieved values, and not a whim.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the definition to its job.

pairs.right: Names the source and the order

feedback.note: Three pieces do the work of the unit. Treating happiness as a stored object is outside the definition.

exercises.prompt: Restore the three key words.

feedback.note: State, values, and whim are the three words. Object and luck are extras in the bank.

exercises.prompt: Build the whole definition.

feedback.note: Happiness is the state from achieved values. Whims and rumors stay out of the built sentence.

exercises.prompt: A friend remembers only not a whim. What is still missing?

choices.text: That it is the emotional state following achieved values
Nothing. The refusal is the entire definition.
A statute number
That happiness means the loss of every value

feedback.note: Not a whim is only the refusal. The positive claim is still the emotional state that follows achieved values.

exercises.prompt: Match the incomplete memory to what it leaves out.

pairs.right: Leaves out achieved values and the whim refusal
Leaves out that happiness is the state that follows

feedback.note: Each fragment is real, and none of them is the whole unit by itself.

exercises.prompt: Complete the summary line.

parts.text: Happiness follows from achieved values, not from a

feedback.note: The contrast at the end of the summary is a whim. Value and state are the other side of the definition, not the thing it is not.

exercises.prompt: Which change would break the definition?

choices.text: Replacing achieved values with a whim
Keeping happiness as an emotional state
Letting the state follow the achievement
Denying that happiness is a whim

feedback.note: Swap the source for a whim and the unit’s definition is gone. The other three choices are the definition itself.

exercises.prompt: Build the refusal that closes the definition.

feedback.note: The closing refusal is not as a whim. State, value, and always are not part of that short line.

exercises.prompt: You finish the unit. Which check shows you have the idea?

choices.text: You can say state, achieved values, and not a whim without dropping one
You remember only the word whim
You treat every mood as happiness
You skip values and keep the feeling alone

feedback.note: The check is the whole definition together: an emotional state, from achieved values, and not a whim.
